lessons.claim: The orientational relaxation time of a dilute axisymmetric-particle suspension is 1/(6 Dr) -- neither 1/Dr nor 1/(2Dr). The loss term is De/(36+De^2) (De=omega/Dr) so the pole is at De=6, and this function is exactly the same as a single Maxwell mode with lambda=1/(6Dr) up to one proportionality constant (deviation <1e-12). That is, this system's linear viscoelasticity is exactly a single Maxwell mode. ★ But the 6 is the coefficient of the 3D l=2 (stress) mode, so applying it to a first moment or to a 2D angular correlation (abp-rod's <cos dtheta>) is wrong

not_verified: the 2D coefficient was not confirmed from this book
